From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: DeepDive Health — post-call recap: network boundary questions & compliance drivers

Samira / Jordan — thanks again for the quick call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a consolidated list of asks so we can scope a follow-up technical session with your infra and security teams.

Summary of what we heard
- Compliance driver: you mentioned a regulatory requirement that effectively mandates air-gapped or demonstrably isolated hosting for PHI processing; primary goal is to avoid any uncontrolled egress to the public internet.
- Residency: data must remain within DeepDive Health's AWS account/region (us-east-1) and be fully auditable.
- Network constraints: no outbound traffic except to a small set of IPs via private peering (no NAT->public internet).
- Ops constraint: minimal ability to run vendor-managed agents on customer infra; preference is for a VPC-resident deployment (Private with strict egress control) or on-prem appliance if VPC approaches are blocked.
- Workload: bursty inference with peaks up to ~300 reqs/min per 2k-token request (rough estimate) and long tail retention for KV cache while preserving tenant isolation.

Immediate asks / next steps (what we can do next week)
1) Please share an initial network diagram (CIDR ranges, transit gateways, any firewall/NAT boxes) — attach to reply if possible.
2) Confirm whether outbound connectivity to an AWS PrivateLink endpoint is allowed, or if only VPC peering/private transit is acceptable.
3) Provide the compliance owner we should loop in (name + email) so we can route security artifacts and a short SOC/Security packet.
4) Schedule a dedicated technical deep-dive with your infra + security folks (30–45m). We propose Mon/Tue next week; LMK availability.

Attachments: we will attach a short reference diagram showing the two deployment options (VPC PrivateLink vs on-prem appliance) and a one-page checklist for egress controls.

Thanks — I captured action items below and will follow up in HubSpot.

Chloe Martin

Thanks Chloe — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Compliance context: we're governed by HIPAA controls with additional enterprise policy that prefers an air-gap-like model for any third-party inference that touches PHI. Practically that means we cannot have uncontrolled egress; approved patterns are VPC peering, PrivateLink, or an on-prem deployment inside our datacenter.
- Connectivity specifics: we can do VPC peering inside AWS (us-east-1) but all egress must flow through our perimeter firewall. PrivateLink is acceptable but we need to validate DNS and certs with our infra team.
- Ports/protocols: at a minimum we'll need TCP 443 outbound to PrivateLink endpoints or specific IP ranges if peering is used. No SSH access permitted into our production VPCs.
- Throughput: rough peak numbers are what you wrote; we will follow up with more precise RPS/ps per route.

I'll attach the security questionnaire and our internal network diagram (redacted). Please note: the compliance owner for this evaluation is Jordan Lee (jordan.lee@deepdivehealth.com), VP of IT Governance. Loop him into the technical deep-dive.

Samira
Chief Product Officer
DeepDive Health
samira@deepdivehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0107

Subject: Re: DeepDive Health — post-call recap: network boundary questions & compliance drivers — technical checklist

Samira / Jordan — Marcus here (Solutions Engineering). Short technical checklist and initial feasibility notes for the deep-dive:

1) Connectivity patterns we can support (short):
   - PrivateLink endpoint (preferred for managed-hosted option): inbound to a PrivateLink inside your VPC, TLS mutual auth supported, DNS override OK in most cases.
   - VPC peering with egress control: we can deploy inside your account and sit behind your perimeter firewall, but peering requires route table changes and you to expose a small set of subnets.
   - On-prem appliance (air-gapped): we ship a hardened runtime image; requires physical or virtual host with GPU/CPU profile we can confirm after throughput numbers.

2) Info we need from you to scope next steps:
   - CIDR ranges and whether you have a dedicated transit VPC (sample CIDRs are fine).
   - Expected sustained/peak tokens per second and concurrency by route (estimates are fine).
   - KMS requirements: do you require a CMK and HSM-backed KMS?
   - Audit obligations: retention windows for logs and whether logs must stay in your account.

3) Preliminary risk notes:
   - If you need zero-e% outbound to public internet, PrivateLink is the faster path for a hosted but VPC-resident option.
   - On-prem appliance will increase delivery timeline and procurement, but it solves the strictest air-gap/approval workflows.

Attaching a short architecture sketch and a one-page runbook stub to help your infra team evaluate impact. Happy to run the 45m technical session and demo a minimal end-to-end handshake.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
